is: The application layer (DD 55836674): one `#[use_case]` method per use case on a per-entity namespace (`Accounts`, `Commissions`, `Users`, `Characters`), called by every driver (api, cli), holding orchestration between routing and domain — organized as `account/` and `commission/` entity trees, the flat `user` and `character` modules, and the `transaction()` orchestrator for callers that are not use-case methods.
conventions: One `#[use_case] pub async fn` per use case, a method on its namespace (`app.accounts().role().grant(cmd)`), no mediator.

Each use case is its own file exporting `Command` (or `Query`) + `Output` + the `impl Namespace<'_>` block holding the method; sub-facets (`account::invitation`, `commission::deadline::status`, …) nest as directories of such files under the parent module.

Parameter order: `&self`, `#[ports] ports: &Ports`, `#[unit] uow: Unit<'_>`, then the caller's params. The macro strips the injected ones from the public signature, so drivers pass only `cmd`/`query`, runtime config and `now`.

A write takes `#[unit]`: the generated wrapper opens the unit before the body, commits on `Ok`, rolls back on `Err`. A read takes `#[ports]` only. `clippy.toml` bans a hand-written `begin`/`commit`/`rollback` in this crate, tests included.

A namespace is a struct deriving `macros::WithPorts`: a root holds `#[ports(is_root = true)] ports: &'a Ports`, a facet holds `#[ports]` on a reference to its parent and gets its accessor on the parent for free.
The module root file keeps the namespace, the terse-`Display` error enum (never interpolates the cause — it stays on `source()`) and the `Result` alias.
Runtime config + `now: DateTimeUtc` are plain params.
Output DTOs carry domain VALUES, never entities.
The dependency floor is witnessed by `tests/dep_guard.rs`.
A use case need not have an actor: `commission::sweep_deadlines` is the system acting on an injected `now` — a free fn over `transaction()`, since `#[use_case]` needs `self`.

notes: The composition root assembles ONE `Ports` bag (`app.rs`); `App` vends the root namespaces `Accounts`/`Commissions`/`Users` with the ports already bound, and drivers pass only `now`. Every `Ports` entry is required, so `MissingPort` is currently unreachable — it is the home for the first port a driver profile may omit.

`transaction()` commits on `Ok` and rolls back on `Err` — the same bracket the `#[use_case]` wrapper inlines. It takes a bare `&dyn Database`, so `sweep_deadlines`, `composition::Runtime::transaction` and the test seeders share it; its three disallowed-method calls are the only ones left in `src/`, under an `#[allow]` with its reason. (DD 24150017)

Its closure bound is `domain::ports::UnitOfWorkFn` plus explicit `F: Send`/`T: Send`, NOT std's `AsyncFnOnce` — higher-ranked `AsyncFnOnce` bounds do not hold the returned future `Send` (rust-lang/rust#110338).

Each module's `From<anyhow::Error>` impl is the single place a typed store error becomes a use-case error; `?` is the only path a store error takes, so no call site can let a 404/409 degrade into a 500.
Authorization posture across the crate: refusals never distinguish "absent" from "forbidden" for a caller with no standing. See the per-module NODE.json notes.
See also: ZMVP-205 — the application-layer restructure that moved use cases below the HTTP layer (tests/dep_guard.rs, tests/user.rs, tests/account.rs, tests/commission.rs, tests/commission_files.rs).

Because the unit opens before the body, it spans everything the body does — including the external calls in `account/create` and `character/create` (DID mint), `account/change_handle` (DID-document update) and `commission/files/upload` (blob write), and the early-return paths that used to leave before `begin`.

Three use-case files carry no `#[use_case]` because they inject nothing: `account/facts/exist.rs` (stub), `character/delete.rs` (`todo!()`), `commission/status/direction/clear.rs` (delegates to `set`).
A use-case file whose namespace has no inherent `ports()` imports `crate::ports::WithPorts`: the `#[unit]` wrapper calls `self.ports()` by method syntax.
